plan.chapterName: Anton, Bivens, and Davis. Calculus, 10th Edition, Figure 14.2.9
plan.contextChunk: This figure is part of a worked example asking to evaluate the double integral of (2x - y^2) over the triangular region R enclosed between y = -x + 1, y = x + 1, and y = 3. The figure shows the triangular region R in the xy-plane with vertices at (-2, 3), (0, 1), and (2, 3); the bounding lines y = 3 (top), y = -x + 1 (lower left), and y = x + 1 (lower right) are labeled. The y-axis divides R into two sub-regions: R1 (shaded blue, left half) and R2 (shaded yellow, right half), each with a red vertical strip indicating the direction of inner integration. The figure illustrates the decomposition of R into two type-I sub-regions required when the lower boundary changes expression across the y-axis.

interactionPlan.concept: When the lower boundary of a region changes formula across the slicing direction, the double integral must be split into separate Type-I sub-integrals at that change point — and the split disappears if the slicing direction is reversed.
elements: x-axis with arrow, tick marks and labels at -2, 0, and 2
y-axis with arrow, labeled y
triangular region R with vertices (-2, 3), (0, 1), and (2, 3), outlined in blue
top boundary line y = 3, labeled 'y = 3' above both the left and right halves
lower-left boundary line y = -x + 1, labeled to the left of the region
lower-right boundary line y = x + 1, labeled to the right of the region
sub-region R1 (left of y-axis), shaded light blue, labeled R1
sub-region R2 (right of y-axis), shaded light yellow/tan, labeled R2
red vertical strip marker inside R1 and inside R2 indicating the inner (Type I) integration direction
blue horizontal strip marker spanning R (visible only in Type II view)
live annotation showing the inner integral limits for R1 and R2 as the boundary equations are edited

interactions.label: Lower boundary equations
interactions.teaches: The split at x = 0 and the two sets of inner integration limits come directly from the lower boundary having different formulas on each side of the y-axis — editing either equation redraws that boundary, reshapes R1 or R2, and updates the integral limits, showing the decomposition is a consequence of the formula change, not of the region's shape alone

interactions.label: Slice direction
interactions.teaches: Switching to horizontal (Type II) slices covers all of R in one continuous sweep from the left boundary to the right boundary, removing the need to decompose R into R1 and R2 at all

demo_steps.title: Why the region splits
demo_steps.narration: With vertical slices, the lower boundary is y = -x + 1 on the left and y = x + 1 on the right — two different formulas — so R must be decomposed into R1 and R2 at x = 0, each with its own inner integral.

demo_steps.title: Edit a boundary equation
demo_steps.narration: Change one of the lower boundary equations and watch that boundary line redraw, the shaded sub-region reshape, and the displayed inner integral limits update — the split exists because the formula changes, and it follows wherever that change occurs.

demo_steps.title: Avoid the split entirely
demo_steps.narration: Toggle to horizontal slices: a single strip sweeps from the left line to the right line across all of R, so one integral with limits x = -(y - 1) to x = (y - 1) covers the whole region — no decomposition needed.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: A double integral must be split wherever the boundary's formula changes along the slicing direction — and choosing the perpendicular slicing direction can eliminate the split entirely.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Match the textbook layout: axes centered in the lower half of the canvas, x-axis tick labels -2, 0, 2 below the axis, y-axis labeled with an arrow. The triangle points downward — apex at (0, 1) sitting just above the origin on the y-axis, base along y = 3 from (-2, 3) to (2, 3) — with a medium-blue outline. R1 filled light blue, R2 filled pale yellow/tan, with italic serif labels R1 and R2 centered in each half. Red vertical strips sit midway inside each half, running from the slanted lower boundary up to y = 3. Boundary labels in italic serif math styling: 'y = 3' appears twice above the top edge (left and right of the y-axis), 'y = -x + 1' to the left of the region, 'y = x + 1' to the right. In Type II mode, hide the red strips and the R1/R2 shading distinction and show one blue horizontal strip spanning the full width of R; cross-fade between modes. A small annotation panel near the figure displays the current inner integral limits, updating live as the boundary equations are edited.
